Principal Component Analysis of Acoustic Impulse Responses

Discovering Interpretable Latent Dimensions

January 2026 | 115 IRs from EchoThief Library

Abstract

We investigate whether PCA can discover interpretable perceptual dimensions in acoustic impulse responses. Using 115 real-world IRs, we compare SVD on raw waveforms vs. PCA on acoustic features. Feature-based PCA successfully recovers three interpretable axes—clarity, brightness, and bass—capturing 85% of variance. Raw SVD spreads variance thinly (31% in 10 PCs) and correlates with recording artifacts rather than room acoustics.

Key Results

Main Finding: 3 acoustic features explain 85% of IR variation:
  1. Clarity (53%) — dry/direct ↔ wet/reverberant
  2. Brightness (26%) — dark ↔ bright spectrum
  3. Bass Content (7%) — boomy ↔ thin

Conclusion

Raw SVD on IR waveforms does NOT yield interpretable acoustic dimensions. It captures recording artifacts (microphone response, gain) rather than room properties.
Feature-based PCA successfully discovers 3 perceptual axes: Clarity, Brightness, and Bass—capturing 85% of acoustic variation with just 3 numbers.

Implication: For reverb parameterization, use acoustic features (RT60, C80, spectral centroid), not raw waveforms.
